Check each: an acute isosceles triangle that is not equilateral has no right angle and has two equal sides; an acute scalene triangle has no right angle and does not have two equal sides; a right scalene triangle has a right angle and does not have two equal sides; a right isosceles triangle has a right angle and has two equal sides. Of these, only a right scalene triangle meets the hypothesis and misses the conclusion. (A case where the hypothesis fails says nothing about the statement, whatever the conclusion does.) So a right scalene triangle.
